subject: Residency evacuation: control-plane evacuation slates & operational authorizations
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sven Müller <sven.muller@acmebank.de>, Priyanka Sharma <priyanka@fintechasia.co>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Residency evacuation: control-plane evacuation slates & operational authorizations

Team / Sven / Priyanka —

We have a narrow window to validate the control-plane evacuation plan for the EU->APAC private deployment (Acme Bank pilot + Fintech Asia staging). I want to collect the final operational "slates" (runbook fragments + network authorizations) we will use in the emergency cutover test on 2027-06-18. Specifically please provide the following by EOD Monday: 

- Marissa: BGP peering auth table and the expected origination ACL change that will run during failover. CSV format preferred.
- Rishi: the trimmed runbook steps we will allow on the console (max 12 steps) — include rollback bullets.
- Neha: confirmation on KMS key access and cross-region audit-log retention window.
- Jonas: who will own the approval gate during the test (name + backup).
- Sven / Priyanka: any contractual evidence or additional controls Acme/Fintech require for the evacuation exercise (DocuSign or security addenda).

Attached: evac-checklist-v1.pdf (stub) — contains the test plan outline. I want one consolidated package so we can share with Acme/Fintech by Tue morning.

Thanks — keep things terse here.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: evac-checklist-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 72KB stub)

Subject: Re: Residency evacuation: control-plane evacuation slates & operational authorizations

Sean — quick update and attachment.

I've exported the BGP auth table and the minimal ACLs we'll apply for the cutover. Key notes:
- Peers: eu1-redwood-peer (203.0.113.12) <-> acme-eu-edge (198.51.100.10) — neighbor auth by MD5; table attached (bgp-auth-table.csv).
- We'll remove the east-european egress route only for the duration of the evacuation window (estimated 4–6 minutes) and then re-announce.
- Change window will be automated via our runbook but gated by an approval signal from Jonas.

I've attached the CSV. Also added a short network play excerpt into runbook-evac-slates-v2.md for Rishi to harmonize.

Marissa
Sr. Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: bgp-auth-table.csv (text/csv, 3KB stub)

Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 20:47:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Residency evacuation: control-plane evacuation slates & operational authorizations

Thanks Sean / Marissa —

Two points from Acme security: 
1) We need a signed addendum that outlines key custody responsibilities during the evacuation window (encryption keys, KMS access, and who is permitted to initiate rollbacks). DocuSign is fine.
2) Audit logs for the control-plane operations must be exported to our audit bucket and retained for 90 days by default for this test. We will accept a signed commitment that logs are not truncated.

I'll have legal send the bullet points to Priyanka and Sean. For the runbook, please make sure the BGP MD5 secret is not embedded in any shared doc — we will exchange it via a secure channel.

—Sven
Sven Müller
Head of Platform Security, Acme Bank
sven.muller@acmebank.de

Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 00:22:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: Residency evacuation: control-plane evacuation slates & operational authorizations

Folks —

I've taken Marissa's excerpts and produced a condensed runbook (runbook-evac-slates-v2.md attached). Key highlights:
- 10-step automated procedure for evacuation: pre-flight validations -> announce withdrawal -> route swap -> health-probe verification -> metric check -> re-announce. Each step has an explicit rollback guard.
- Rollback matrix: immediate rollback on CPU/tailer latency breach (>250ms p50 increase) or failed probes for 3 consecutive checks.
- We will NOT store BGP secrets in the runbook. Secrets will be passed using our secure vault channel (vault.redwood.com transfer ticket).
- Ops gate: Jonas Weber (owner), backup: Neha Kapoor. Jonas must send the approval token (console UI) and Neha must acknowledge in Slack.

I'll queue an internal dry-run on Friday and invite Jonas + Neha.

—Rishi
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: runbook-evac-slates-v2.md (text/markdown, 12KB stub)
Attachment note: secrets handled via secure vault — see runbook for ticket workflow.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sven Müller <sven.muller@acmebank.de>, Priyanka Sharma <priyanka@fintechasia.co>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 01:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Residency evacuation: control-plane evacuation slates & operational authorizations

Appreciate the fast turnarounds. Final action items (for distribution to Acme / Fintech):

1) Marissa: confirm the CSV contains anonymized neighbor secrets and that the actual MD5 keys will be exchanged over the vault channel.
2) Rishi: deliver final runbook and include the dry-run results summary after Friday.
3) Neha: confirm KMS cross-region access window and that audit-logs will be exported to acme-audit-bucket for 90 days.
4) Jonas: be prepared to issue the console approval token during the 06/18 test; provide backup contact (Neha).
5) Sven / Priyanka: legal addendum (DocuSign) is required to capture custody and retention commitments — please send the initial bullet list and we will convert to a short addendum.

I'll package the attachments and send a single packet to Acme/Fintech first thing Monday. If anyone sees risk not covered by the runbook or BGP plan, flag it here.

—Sean
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Attachment: signed-docusign-acme.pdf (application/pdf, 110KB stub)
